marajoara-culture.name: Marajoara culture
marajoara-culture.summary: An ancient culture that flourished on Marajó island at the mouth of the Amazon in Brazil, with human activity documented as early as 1000 BCE.

maraj.name: Marajó
maraj.summary: A large island in Pará, Brazil, at the mouth of the Amazon, site from roughly 400 BCE to 1600 CE of the advanced pre-Cabraline Marajoara society.

guaran-people.name: Guaraní people
guaran-people.summary: An indigenous South American people, numbering around 280,000, living mainly in Paraguay, Argentina, Brazil and Bolivia, whose language remains an official language of Paraguay.

maloca.name: Maloca
maloca.summary: Traditional Amazonian long house shared by several families, with separate entrances for men and women and space cleared for ceremonial dances.

terra-preta.name: Terra preta
terra-preta.summary: A dark, fertile soil found in the Amazon Basin, created by indigenous farmers mixing charcoal, bones, pottery and manure into naturally poor soil, and remaining fertile for thousands of years.

tupinamb-people.name: Tupinambá
tupinamb-people.summary: A Tupi ethnic group that lived along Brazil's Atlantic coast before Portuguese colonization, whose name was also applied to other related Tupi-speaking groups; their language survives as Nheengatu.

mapuche.name: Mapuche
mapuche.summary: An Indigenous people of south-central Chile and southwestern Argentina, with a traditional economy based on agriculture and material culture known for textiles and silverwork.

lonko.name: Lonko
lonko.summary: A chief of Mapuche communities, typically among the wealthier men, who governed alongside war leaders called toki elected in wartime.

arauco-peninsula.name: Arauco Peninsula
arauco-peninsula.summary: A peninsula in southern Chile projecting northwest into the Pacific Ocean, west of the Cordillera de Nahuelbuta.

charles-c-mann.name: Charles C. Mann
charles-c-mann.summary: American journalist and author (born 1955) whose 2006 book on the pre-Columbian Americas won a major book award.

acre-geoglyphs.name: Acre geoglyphs
acre-geoglyphs.summary: Ancient excavated earth structures in Brazil's Acre state, called 'earth tattoos' by local Indigenous groups; one is dated to about 2,500 years old.

biob-o-region.name: Biobío Region
biob-o-region.summary: One of Chile's sixteen administrative regions, home to about 1.5 million people and containing the major city of Concepción.

neuqu-n-province.name: Neuquén Province
neuqu-n-province.summary: A province of Argentina in the west of the country, at the northern end of Patagonia, bordering Chile.

tupi-people.name: Tupi people
tupi-people.summary: One of the largest Indigenous groups in Brazil before European colonization, who migrated from the Amazon and settled along the Atlantic coast beginning around 1,000 years ago.

tupiniquim.name: Tupiniquim
tupiniquim.summary: An Indigenous Tupi people of Brazil, today living in three Indigenous territories near Aracruz in Espírito Santo state; a 2010 census counted 2,630 of them.

potiguara.name: Potiguara
potiguara.summary: An Indigenous people of Brazil, today living in about 26 villages in Paraíba; their name means "shrimp-eaters" in the Tupi language.

mapudungun.name: Mapudungun
mapudungun.summary: The language of the Mapuche people, spoken in south-central Chile and west-central Argentina, with no official national status in either country.

yvy-mar-e.name: Yvy marã e'ỹ
yvy-mar-e.summary: A mythical paradise in Guarani mythology, meaning 'land without evils,' free of hunger, wars or disease.

tau-mythology.name: Tau
tau-mythology.summary: An evil spirit in Guaraní mythology, created by the supreme god Tupã alongside his opposite, Angatupyry, and left with humanity on Earth.

antu-mapuche-mythology.name: Antu
antu-mapuche-mythology.summary: The principal sun spirit in Mapuche mythology, representing light, wisdom and spirit, and married to Kueyen, the moon spirit.

tupi-language.name: Old Tupi
tupi-language.summary: The classical language of Brazil's Indigenous Tupi people, used as a lingua franca in colonial Brazil and having a rich literary tradition before being suppressed; its only surviving descendant is Nheengatu.

kuhikugu.name: Kuhikugu
kuhikugu.summary: Archaeological site in the Brazilian Amazon at the headwaters of the Xingu River, showing evidence of large, sophisticated ancient settlements.

inter-caetera.name: Inter caetera
inter-caetera.summary: A 1493 papal bull by Pope Alexander VI granting Spain's monarchs all lands west and south of a line drawn near the Azores and Cape Verde islands.

treaty-of-tordesillas.name: Treaty of Tordesillas
treaty-of-tordesillas.summary: 1494 treaty dividing newly discovered lands outside Europe between Portugal and Castile along a meridian west of Cape Verde.

maule-river.name: Maule River
maule-river.summary: A major Chilean river tied to the country's Inca-era, colonial and independence history, which marked the Inca Empire's southern frontier.

itata-river.name: Itata River
itata-river.summary: A river in southern Chile's Ñuble Region that marked the historical boundary between the Mapuche to the south and the Picunche to the north.

maipo-river.name: Maipo River
maipo-river.summary: River flowing near Santiago, Chile, with headwaters in the Andes, historically marking part of the Inca Empire's southern frontier.

pedro-lvares-cabral.name: Pedro Álvares Cabral
pedro-lvares-cabral.summary: Portuguese nobleman and navigator (c. 1467–c. 1520) regarded as the European discoverer of Brazil, leading a 1500 expedition that touched four continents.

tupi-guarani-languages.name: Tupi–Guarani languages
tupi-guarani-languages.summary: The most widely distributed subfamily of Tupian languages in South America, about fifty languages including Guarani and Old Tupi; modern Guarani is an official language of Paraguay.

mitma.name: Mitma
mitma.summary: An Inca policy of forcibly resettling whole communities to newly conquered lands to spread loyalty and Inca culture, affecting roughly a quarter to a third of the empire's population.

pukara.name: Pukara
pukara.summary: A fortified hilltop site built by pre-Hispanic Andean peoples, emerging widely between about 1000 and 1430 CE and later adopted by the Inca military in contested border areas.

jos-bengoa.name: José Bengoa
jos-bengoa.summary: Chilean historian and anthropologist (1945–2026) known for his studies of Mapuche history and society, dismissed from his university post after the 1973 coup.

vicente-y-ez-pinz-n.name: Vicente Yáñez Pinzón
vicente-y-ez-pinz-n.summary: A Spanish navigator, youngest of the Pinzón brothers, who captained the Niña alongside Columbus on his first voyage to the New World in 1492.

cabo-de-santo-agostinho.name: Cape of Santo Agostinho
cabo-de-santo-agostinho.summary: A coastal area in Pernambuco, Brazil, reached by Spanish navigator Vicente Yáñez Pinzón in January 1500, though Brazil's official discovery is credited to Pedro Álvares Cabral later that year.

pernambuco.name: Pernambuco
pernambuco.summary: A state in northeastern Brazil, named after a colonial captaincy established in 1534, with its capital at Recife and a strong African-influenced culture.

osvaldo-silva.name: Osvaldo Silva
osvaldo-silva.summary: Chilean historian of prehistory (1940–2019) who founded academic history journals and proposed a different chronology for Inca rule in Chile.

mapuche-religion.name: Ngünechen
mapuche-religion.summary: One of the most prominent deities in Mapuche religion, sometimes equated with the Christian God.

pillan.name: Pillán
pillan.summary: Powerful, respected spirits in Mapuche mythology said to cause disasters such as earthquakes and floods, or to grant benefits; the most powerful, Antü, governs the rest.

kueyen.name: Kueyen
kueyen.summary: Moon spirit in Mapuche mythology, chief among the star spirits and wife of Antu, the sun spirit.

huilliche-people.name: Huilliche
huilliche-people.summary: The southern branch of the Mapuche people of Chile and Argentina, who successfully resisted Spanish encroachment for centuries before their defeat in 1792.

tiwanaku.name: Tiwanaku
tiwanaku.summary: A major pre-Columbian archaeological site in Bolivia near Lake Titicaca, home to an estimated 10,000 to 20,000 people around 800 CE, with monumental structures and megalithic stonework.

martin-dobrizhoffer.name: Martin Dobrizhoffer
martin-dobrizhoffer.summary: Austrian Roman Catholic missionary and writer (1717–1791).

chicha.name: Chicha
chicha.summary: A traditional Andean and Amazonian beverage, most commonly a corn beer called chicha de jora, used ceremonially in the Inca Empire.

diaguita.name: Diaguita
diaguita.summary: An Indigenous people of Chile and Argentina, politically fragmented into several chiefdoms; their archaeological culture emerged around 1000 CE, known for irrigation systems and painted pottery.

temuco.name: Temuco
temuco.summary: A city in southern Chile founded from an 1881 fort during Chile's conquest of Araucanía, at the heart of the traditional Mapuche homeland.

tabajara.name: Tabajara
tabajara.summary: An Indigenous people of Brazil's northeastern Atlantic coast before and during Portuguese colonization, whose name means 'lord of the village' in Tupi-Guarani.

las-nimas-complex.name: Las Ánimas complex
las-nimas-complex.summary: An archaeological culture of northern Chile's Norte Chico region, developing between 800 and 1000 CE as the immediate precursor to the Diaguita culture.

el-molle-culture.name: El Molle culture
el-molle-culture.summary: A South American archaeological culture of Chile's Norte Chico region, known for its ceramics, that existed from 300 to 700 CE before being replaced by the Las Ánimas culture.
